subject: ophthalmology
title: Posterior uveitis, panuveitis and endophthalmitis

steps.tx: **Intermediate uveitis**, also called **pars planitis**, fills the inferior vitreous with snowball opacities and snowbank exudates over the pars plana in young adults, and it is often idiopathic but associated with multiple sclerosis, sarcoidosis or Lyme disease. **Cystoid macular oedema** causes the central blurring, so control persistent oedema with periocular or systemic steroids plus immunosuppression, and consider pars plana vitrectomy to clear debris in selected cases. Ask about white matter symptoms because the multiple sclerosis link needs neurology review.
steps.say: Snowball opacities hanging low in the vitreous with snowbank exudates in a young adult mean intermediate uveitis, so ask about multiple sclerosis, sarcoidosis and Lyme disease. Central blurring comes from cystoid macular oedema, which needs periocular or systemic steroids with immunosuppression when it persists. Debris that refuses to clear may need pars plana vitrectomy in selected cases.

steps.tx: **Toxoplasmosis** causes the commonest infectious posterior uveitis, with recurrent focal necrotising retinochoroiditis beside old pigmented scars forming satellite lesions, plus overlying vitritis that looks like a headlight in fog. Treat active edges with pyrimethamine plus sulfadiazine with folinic rescue and add steroids only alongside effective cover, using specialist regimens in pregnancy and immunocompromise. **Cytomegalovirus retinitis** shows haemorrhagic pizza pie necrosis in AIDS with low CD4 counts, while acute retinal necrosis brings herpetic peripheral whitening and ocular tuberculosis completes the infectious set.
steps.say: A fresh fluffy retinal edge beside an old pigmented scar in foggy vitreous means toxoplasmosis, so start antiparasitic treatment before adding steroids. Pregnancy and immunocompromise need specialist regimens with careful cover. Haemorrhagic pizza pie necrosis in AIDS with low CD4 counts points to cytomegalovirus, while herpetic peripheral whitening means acute retinal necrosis.

steps.tx: **Behcet disease** pairs oral with genital ulcers plus hypopyon uveitis and retinal vasculitis in silk route populations, and it needs aggressive immunosuppression with biologics to prevent blinding occlusions. **Vogt Koyanagi Harada disease** brings bilateral exudative detachments with disc swelling, vitiligo, poliosis and meningismus after a viral prodrome in pigmented races, and it needs prolonged high dose steroids with steroid sparing agents to prevent sunset glow fundus. Sympathetic ophthalmia and sarcoid panuveitis join the bilateral granulomatous set, and fluorescein angiography maps vasculitis and ischaemia to guide laser.
steps.say: Mouth ulcers with genital ulcers and hypopyon uveitis mean Behcet disease, which needs aggressive immunosuppression with biologics to prevent blinding occlusions. Vitiligo with bilateral exudative detachments and disc swelling after a viral prodrome points to Vogt Koyanagi Harada disease, which needs prolonged high dose steroids. Fluorescein angiography maps the vasculitis and guides laser treatment.

steps.tx: This paired image shows **Behcet disease** in two views. The angiogram displays bright **vascular leakage** from inflamed retinal vessels with dark nonperfused **ischaemic zones**, which explain why aggressive immunosuppression must prevent blinding occlusions. The clinical photo shows **hypopyon** uveitis with layered pus settling inferiorly, which marks severe anterior inflammation. Linking leakage with hypopyon helps you recognise Behcet in the exam.
steps.say: The angiogram shows bright leakage from inflamed retinal vessels with dark zones where perfusion is lost, which explains why Behcet disease threatens vision through occlusions. The clinical photo shows layered pus settling at the bottom of the anterior chamber, which marks severe hypopyon uveitis. When leakage pairs with hypopyon ulcers, you should recognise Behcet disease and start aggressive immunosuppression.

steps.tx: **Endophthalmitis** follows surgery, trauma, infected blebs or septic emboli in diabetics and immunosuppressed patients, and it declares itself with pain, crashing vision, lid swelling, hypopyon and dense vitritis that obscures the fundus. Start with urgent **vitreous tap** plus **intravitreal antibiotics** with vancomycin and ceftazidime and consider early vitrectomy for severe postoperative cases, since sterile inflammation and toxic syndromes lack this dense vitritis. Prevent cases with povidone iodine preparation and intracameral antibiotics at cataract surgery.
steps.say: Pain with crashing vision and no fundus view after surgery or trauma means endophthalmitis, so tap the vitreous and inject intravitreal antibiotics at once. Early vitrectomy helps severe postoperative cases, while sterile inflammation lacks dense vitritis. Povidone iodine preparation with intracameral antibiotics at cataract surgery prevents most cases.
